phase: Phase 15: AEGIS End-to-End Integrity, Security & Claim Audit

verified_fixes.vulnerability: SecurityEnforcementEngine lacked verification of automated_blocking_allowed on approved actions
verified_fixes.fix: Added strict policy check raising PermissionError and recording status='BLOCKED_BY_POLICY' when automated actions target UNKNOWN_OR_REVIEW incidents without SOC_ANALYST identity

verified_fixes.vulnerability: response_generation_agent defaulted to FIREWALL_DROP even when incident was abstained/untrusted
verified_fixes.fix: Replaced disruptive mitigation with non-disruptive forensic PCAP capture and telemetry monitoring for abstained incidents

verified_fixes.vulnerability: LLMSynthesizer declared incidents as confirmed attacks without exposing UNKNOWN/advisory status
verified_fixes.fix: Tagged syntheses of abstained alerts with [FACT / ABSTAINED] header, warning that attack classification is advisory and automated blocking is prohibited

recommendations.title: Enforce Dynamic Edge Ingress Rate-Limiting & SYN Cookie Protection
recommendations.rationale: Advisory only. Retrieved DDoS-relevant guidance supports availability protection: [General context — NIST NIST SP 800-53: Control SC-5 (Denial-of-Service Protection)]: Implement boundary protection, ingress rate-limiting, SYN cookies, and adaptive traffic throttling at the IoT network gateway to restrict volumetric flood attacks and maintain availability of cr
recommendations.precautions: Avoid hard dropping entire subnets if mixed benign/malicious traffic shares the ingress port. Human-in-the-loop approval required.
recommendations.guidance: If supported by retrieved controls: deploy per-source rate-limiting and TCP SYN cookies at the border. Do not treat this as confirmed for this flow until an analyst reviews the evidence.
supporting_sources: CISA (CISA Advisory AA22-110A: Defending IoT and OT Devices Against State-Sponsored and Botnet Threats) [attack_specific]

recommendations.title: Quarantine Affected IoT Gateway Segment via Micro-Segmentation
recommendations.rationale: Advisory isolation guidance from retrieved DDoS/availability context. Not an automated action.
recommendations.precautions: Ensure quarantine VLAN maintains telemetry logging for post-incident forensic replay.
recommendations.guidance: If retrieved playbooks support it: migrate the affected gateway port to a telemetry quarantine VLAN with human oversight.
supporting_sources: CISA (CISA Advisory AA22-110A: Defending IoT and OT Devices Against State-Sponsored and Botnet Threats) [attack_specific]

recommendations.title: Enforce Connection Timeouts and Socket Quotas
recommendations.rationale: Advisory only. Retrieved DoS-relevant guidance (resource/service exhaustion) supports connection protection: Not established from retrieved evidence.
recommendations.precautions: Do not set keep-alive timeouts lower than standard sensor polling intervals without analyst review.
recommendations.guidance: If supported by retrieved controls: tighten idle-connection timeouts and restrict concurrent half-open connections per client.

recommendations.title: Filter Malformed and Unexpected Flag Bursts
recommendations.rationale: Advisory filtering consistent with retrieved endpoint/application exhaustion context. TreeSHAP values are model facts, not proof of a specific packet-crafting technique.
recommendations.precautions: Verify application-layer IoT protocols (MQTT/CoAP) before enforcing header drops.
recommendations.guidance: If retrieved controls support it: configure stateful inspection to drop unexpected flag bursts lacking handshake context.

recommendations.title: Enable Dynamic ARP Inspection (DAI) & DHCP Snooping
recommendations.rationale: Advisory only. Retrieved spoofing/AiTM guidance supports ARP/DHCP controls: NIST (NIST SP 800-53: Control SC-7 (Boundary Protection & Dynamic ARP Inspection)) [attack_specific, acs=0.41]: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 Control SC-7: Boundary Protection & Dynamic ARP Inspection. Guidance: Enforce managed network interfaces, DHCP snooping, Dynamic ARP Inspection (DA
recommendations.precautions: Ensure static IP IoT devices have valid MAC-IP bindings entered in the DHCP snooping database.
recommendations.guidance: If retrieved NIST/CISA excerpts support it: enable DAI and drop unauthorized gratuitous ARPs. Do not infer that this flow already performed ARP poisoning.
supporting_sources: NIST (NIST SP 800-53: Control SC-7 (Boundary Protection & Dynamic ARP Inspection)) [attack_specific]

recommendations.title: Enforce 802.1X Port Authentication & MAC Pinning
recommendations.rationale: Advisory network-access control consistent with retrieved spoofing/boundary-protection evidence.
recommendations.precautions: Confirm critical sensor endpoints support 802.1X or MAC Authentication Bypass (MAB).
recommendations.guidance: If retrieved controls support it: bind switch-port access to authenticated MACs; isolate unverified MACs.
supporting_sources: NIST (NIST SP 800-53: Control SC-7 (Boundary Protection & Dynamic ARP Inspection)) [attack_specific]

critical_final_question.single_biggest_remaining_limitation: Closed-world training coverage: The Mahalanobis OOD detector operates in the 46-dimensional engineered flow feature space of CICIoT2023. While mathematically provable within that manifold, novel stealth attacks whose aggregate flow metrics superficially resemble known DDoS/DoS/Spoofing cluster statistics could slip through without triggering distance thresholds.
